comments.body:
The workflows are showing `action_required` (fork gate) — could a maintainer press "Approve and run workflows"? Local verification so the approval isn't a leap of faith:

- `bundle exec rake internal_investigation` — 126 files, no offenses
- `bundle exec rspec spec/rubocop/cop/performance/squeeze_spec.rb spec/rubocop/cop/performance/delete_prefix_spec.rb spec/rubocop/cop/performance/delete_suffix_spec.rb` — 72 examples, 0 failures
- `bundle exec rspec spec/project_spec.rb` — 71 examples, 0 failures (changelog entry + contributor link)
- The new spec `when the receiver is itself a chained gsub call` fails on `master` (`Parser::ClobberingError`) and passes with the fix.

Ruby 3.4.10, `rubocop` from the `Gemfile.lock`.

The 2nd commit only fills the changelog entry's PR number and adds the `[@pcbeingused333]` link — happy to squash if you'd prefer, though I see PRs here are squash-merged.

Closing — `d41a081` (merged into `master` on 2026-09-06, before this PR was opened) already fixes the exact same crash with the exact same approach: `Performance/Squeeze`'s corrector was replacing the whole node including the receiver, so a chained `gsub` clobbered itself; the fix limits the replacement to `node.loc.selector.join(node.source_range.end)`.

Verified the diffs are equivalent (only the test's receiver variable name differs, `s` vs `str`). No action needed here — thanks for the fast turnaround on this one.
